newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Bimantara cuts car prices.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Bimantara cuts car prices.

text.p: Indonesia's well-diversified PT Bimantara Citra has reduced the sale price of its cars by raising local content, the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Tuesday.
"Because our local content is increasing, automatically we can push down our sales price," Jongkie D. Sugiarto, president-director of Bimantara unit, PT Citra Mobil, was quoted as saying.
Sugiarto was quoted as saying the price of a Cakra had been reduced by 2.5 million rupiah to 37.4 million rupiah and the Nenggala by 3.5 million rupiah to 49.6 million rupiah.
The company said in a statement that local content in the Cakra and Nenggala was at 20.5 percent and 20.7 percent respectively. It did not give comparative data.
Sugiarto said that as a result of higher local content, the import duty on components had been reduced to 50 percent from 65 percent.
He said a 1993 government decree stipulated that the import duty on components would be 50 percent if locally-produced cars contained 20 percent local content.
At 0340 GMT, shares of Bimantara fell 125 rupiah to 4,075 rupiah on a volume of 249,500 shares on what brokers said on profit-taking following sharp gains last week.
Bimantara, controlled by President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo, produces the cars in cooperation with Hyundai Motor Co Ltd.

A company controlled by another son of Suharto, Hutomo Mandala Putra, produces the Timor national car after being granted by tax breaks which are being contested by Japan, the United States and European nations.
